Medicaid's collapse isn't about funding shortages—it's about systemic theft. The Strengthening Medicaid for Serious Mental Illness Act (H.R. 3320) proves the problem: bureaucrats burn billions on duplicate programs and ER misuse while ignoring $55B in annual improper payments. Community health centers shouldn’t foot the bill for D.C.’s failure to secure borders or audit eligibility.

LA’s $3.7B Medicaid budget can’t handle translation services because 48% of residents exploit loopholes instead of assimilating. Real reform means enforcing existing laws, not throwing cash at a broken system.

Prioritize veterans and taxpayers over ER-abusing non-citizens. Audit first, fund second.

I serve on the House Appropriations Committee because that is where bipartisan conversations occur, and I stand ready to work across the aisle to keep our government open, lower costs, expand access to health care, and strengthen our communities.

Rep. Mrvan’s outrage is performative. Indiana’s redistricting push isn’t about “ignoring families”—it’s about dismantling D.C.-aligned bureaucrats who’ve rigged the system for decades. The real scam? Out-of-state PACs and corporate donors (like Paul Singer) bankrolling establishment puppets to keep Hoosiers trapped in a cycle of bloated spending and phony “bipartisan” gridlock.

Braun’s special session aligns with Trump’s America First mandate: root out the Nashville-D.C. machine that prioritizes donor cash over voter interests. While Mrvan clings to his gerrymandered district, Indiana’s grassroots are demanding accountability.

This isn’t politics—it’s war against the uniparty.

The only thing more unpopular in Indiana than redistricting is the Governor himself.  His attempt to silence the very voters he represents is yet another example of how out of touch he is with the people of our great state.

I have spent my career as a public official working on behalf of individuals and families facing economic hardship, often through no fault of their own, who have been in need of access to food, housing, and health care.  Too many times have I witnessed the difficult choice that families often make between choosing between a meal or health care services.  While I appreciate that this legislation will ensure that emergency food assistance will be released as quickly as possible to children, seniors, and individuals with disabilities, it is wrong to do so at the expense of affordable health care benefits.
